clue.text: Care about people

indicators.note: about can mean around in a muddle, so the word before it is turned round into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to look after others, the kind of line on a charity poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a group of humans sharing descent, so it can stand for a people or nation.

clue.text: Everyone else restrains Italian composer after knocking out Dutch preacher

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in check, so the first word grips the second within it

parts.note: the rest means all the others

indicators.note: knocking out a letter removes it from the name before it goes in

parts.note: Antonio Vivaldi, the Venetian composer of The Four Seasons
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A Dutch preacher knocked out while everyone else holds back an Italian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A revivalist is an evangelist who leads religious revival meetings, a kind of preacher.

clue.text: Intimidated women in educational establishment

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the institution that follows

parts.note: a co-ed is a mixed school or college
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Female students left nervous and subdued at their school.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowed means frightened into submission, which is what being intimidated amounts to.

clue.text: Stimulant very good for posh people

parts.note: an upper is slang for a stimulant drug
class as an adjective means excellent, as in a class act

explanation.surface: A remark that pep pills go down well with the smart set.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the stereotype of drug use in high society, which suits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper class is the social stratum of aristocrats and wealthy families, those usually labelled posh in Britain.

clue.text: Summon youngster taking a break

indicators.note: taking means receiving inside, so the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: a pup is a young dog, or slangily a young person
a lucky break is a piece of good fortune

explanation.surface: A child is called in from playtime, taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Break means a stroke of fortune here, not a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck up courage is to summon it, so the phrasal verb matches summon in that sense.

clue.text: Dear me! Lake unusually green

indicators.note: something done unusually is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at how strangely green a lake looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green shade named after the gemstone, so it is a kind of green.

clue.text: Young animal eats filleted solids

parts.note: a young fox, lion or bear

indicators.note: filleting a fish removes its insides, so only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A young animal is fed boned fish as its first solid food.
explanation.walkthrough: Eats looks like the verb of feeding, but it is the word to be filleted.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubes are three-dimensional figures with six square faces, one type of geometric solid.

clue.text: Couple with nearly equal status

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to link or connect one thing to another

definitions.note: describes a rank, as in an associate member, rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the rank just below full membership or partnership

explanation.surface: Pairing up with someone almost your equal in standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate is to join or connect, and an associate professor or member holds a rank just short of full.

clue.text: Tot getting love for wrestling

parts.note: to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A toddler takes a fancy to wrestling.
explanation.walkthrough: Tot suggests a small child, but here it is an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the traditional Japanese style of wrestling between heavyweight competitors.

clue.text: Uproar as British couple house terrorist at centre

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
to ally is to join or couple together
HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: at centre picks out the single middle letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the fifth of its nine letters

explanation.surface: Public outrage as a British couple are found sheltering a terrorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss or sensational publicity, a commotion like an uproar.

clue.text: Promise that's amazing: first wife gets half-cut

indicators.note: the opening letter of the exclamation is the abbreviation for wife, and cutting its written shape in half leaves a different letter

parts.note: an exclamation of astonishment

explanation.surface: A tipsy wedding guest exclaiming over a promise while the first wife gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter W looks like two Vs side by side, so cutting the first W of WOW in half leaves V, giving VOW. Half-cut is also British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A vow is a solemn pledge, the same thing as a promise, as in marriage vows.

clue.text: Please employ escorts in the morning

indicators.note: to escort is to accompany on either side, so one piece goes along wrapped around the other

parts.note: a.m. marks a morning time
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A polite request to hire escorts before noon, rather a racy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Please is a verb here, to delight, not the polite word it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to entertain them, giving them pleasure, so it can replace the verb please.

clue.text: Starmer primarily must stop boom and bust

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this letter goes into the middle of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the leader's name is kept

parts.note: Keir Starmer, the UK Labour leader

explanation.surface: Economic commentary: the prime minister must end the cycle of boom and bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Boom and bust reads as one economic phrase, but bust stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom and bust are both words for a woman's chest, so one noun swaps for the other.

clue.text: Film by Al Gore?

definitions.note: a forename standing for the surname that goes with it

parts.note: short for video
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query about a documentary by the former US vice-president Al Gore.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore suggests the politician, but Gore is the first name of the American novelist Gore Vidal; the question mark flags this definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal was the American writer, so his forename Gore points to his family name.

clue.text: Smack sent back with a cake, occasionally, in backpack

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way, so this word is read from its end

parts.note: to smack someone is to slap them
taken as written

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is used

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A smack in the playground: a child is sent home with a cake stuffed in their school bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a bag carried on the shoulders, the same thing as a backpack or rucksack.

clue.text: Become gnarly and leave!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally to turn twisted and knobbly, like old wood
second meaning: a rude British way of telling someone to go away

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is British slang, a mild version of get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes wood developing knots and, as an insult, tells someone to clear off.

clue.text: Delivery that was mastered by Jonathan Edwards?

definitions.text: Delivery that was mastered by Jonathan Edwards?

parts.note: surface reading: a ball bowled in cricket
setter's reading: Edwards was the British triple jump champion, whose event begins with an extended hop

explanation.surface: A cricket question about a bowling skill, oddly credited to an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a long hop is a short, badly pitched ball that is easy to hit; the triple jump is hop, step and jump, so a jumper's long hop is a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a poor bowling delivery in cricket and, literally, an extended hop in athletics.

clue.text: Uses ninth amendment in military building

indicators.note: an amendment changes a text, so these letters are altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone invokes a constitutional amendment, like pleading the Fifth, about a barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: Ninth amendment suggests the US Bill of Rights, but amendment is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a semicircular corrugated-iron shelter used by the British army as barracks or stores.

clue.text: Duke agreed to change and lower rank

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to reduce in rank

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: the letters are told to change, so they are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aristocrat consents to reform and give up his title.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone originally meant to demote them, stripping them of their grade or position.

clue.text: Shot up in audition — a little shocking

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a child who shot up grew quickly
as in have some

explanation.surface: An actor's sudden growth spurt in an audition is a bit alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot up suggests drug use or a shooting, but it means grew taller.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrifying or ghastly, the sense of shocking applied to grisly sights.

clue.text: Maybe 13 elite servicemen very forward

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 13 across

parts.note: the Special Air Service, the British army's special forces regiment
as in so good
as in moving on

explanation.surface: A soldier's banter: special forces lads being far too forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Vidal Sassoon was the famous British hairdresser, so a Vidal is maybe a Sassoon, as Gore at 13 was a Vidal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-reference gives a forename, and Sassoon is the surname of the stylist who bore that forename.

clue.text: Sped up tempo in Relate events

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a simple past-tense synonym
the speed of a piece

explanation.surface: Things speed up at a session of Relate, the British couples counselling charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Relate is the name of a marriage guidance service, but here it is the verb to recount.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story, recounting a series of happenings in order.

clue.text: Stream entertaining massage for jazz pioneer

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a brook
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A spa by a river, offering massages beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave Brubeck was the American jazz pianist behind Take Five.
explanation.definitionFit: Brubeck led a celebrated quartet and helped pioneer cool jazz and unusual time signatures.

clue.text: Show underwear, and five fuss

parts.note: a bra is a piece of underwear
V is the Roman numeral for five
as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: Someone flashing their underwear, with a group of five kicking up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Show is a noun here, a display of boldness, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a showy display of courage meant to impress, so it is a show of boldness.

clue.text: Pointedly look into Arsenal ignoring odd characters providing services?

definitions.note: describes a place rather than naming it

indicators.note: into places the first piece inside the letters that follow
skipping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters
to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: A football fan glares pointedly at Arsenal's misfits.
explanation.walkthrough: On British motorways a rest area is a service area with fuel, food and toilets, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside rest area is a stopping place that offers drivers services such as fuel and refreshments.

clue.text: Revolutionary again took weapon

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters that follow come out backwards

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
as in sat an exam

explanation.surface: A revolutionary picks up arms once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electroshock gun used by police, a stun weapon that fires darts.

clue.text: Carnivorous couch-dwellers run away, returning for fight

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are read from the end
the run is told to go away, so its abbreviation drops out of the animals' name

parts.note: an otter's den is called a couch, or holt
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Couch potatoes who eat meat flee home and come back, sounding like a family quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Couch-dwellers suggests sofa loafers, but a couch is an otter's lair.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief scrap or quarrel, a British informal word for a fight.

clue.text: Leans close to sexy totty

parts.note: something that leans tips over

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A man leaning in close to an attractive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang totty means attractive women, but it is also an old dialect word for unsteady or dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Totty in its older sense means shaky or fuddled with drink, so it matches slightly drunk.

clue.text: Drunk women briefly making cat cry

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters stagger into a new order
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tipsy women caterwauling into the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Meow, also spelt miaow, is the sound a cat makes, its cry.

clue.text: Get hostelry to stock spirit

indicators.note: a shop that stocks goods holds them inside, so the answer sits within the words before

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to get a pub to stock a particular spirit, like gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit looks like a drink for the pub, but here it means character.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a group or community.

clue.text: Warning from American lecturer with gun, perhaps

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
L is a crossword abbreviation for lecturer
a gun is one kind of firearm, or arm

explanation.surface: An American teacher with a gun issues a warning, a grim campus picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal that alerts people to danger, which is exactly what a warning is.

clue.text: Tap, tap on the counter

indicators.note: counter means opposite, as in counter-clockwise, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tapping twice on a shop counter for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The counter looks like a bar or shop surface, but it tells you to turn the word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pat is a light touch with the hand, much the same as a gentle tap.

clue.text: Musk following Washington call is bearing fruit

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first-named piece is placed at the end

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State
to term something is to call or name it
the forename of the billionaire Elon Musk

explanation.surface: Political news: Musk's role in Washington is finally paying off.
explanation.walkthrough: Musk looks like the scent, but it points to the businessman's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A watermelon is a large, juicy fruit with green rind and red flesh.

clue.text: Couple in Germany converse from sunrise to sunset

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: the converse of something is its opposite, so the period named is read backwards

parts.note: the hours of daylight

explanation.surface: A couple on holiday in Germany chatting all day long.
explanation.walkthrough: Converse looks like a verb for chatting, but it means reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyad is a group of two, a pair, so it can stand for a couple.
